title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 73
paragraphs: All of that happened later. At the time of which I am speaking, Cleomenes — having brought the affair of Demaratus to a successful end — at once took Leotychides with him and marched against the Aeginetans, furious at the insults they had offered him. The Aeginetans, now that both kings had come against them, decided that further resistance was pointless. The Spartans picked out ten of the most prominent men of Aegina, ranked by wealth and by birth, and took them off as prisoners — among them Crios son of Polycritus and Casambus son of Aristocrates, who held the greatest power on the island. Having carried them to Attica, they handed them over for safekeeping to the Athenians, who were Aegina's bitterest enemies.
